message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to current air‑quality data, but you can quickly check the latest conditions in Los Angeles using a few reliable resources:

| Source | What it offers | How to use |
|--------|----------------|------------|
| **AirNow** (EPA) | Current AQI, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO), forecast | Visit <https://www.airnow.gov/> and enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Global map, hourly updates, historical trends | Go to <https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/>. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, CBS Los Angeles) | Often embed live AQI widgets | Search “LA air quality” on their websites. |
| **Mobile apps** (e.g., Plume Labs, BreezoMeter) | Push notifications, health recommendations | Download from App Store / Google Play and enable location services. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities, most of these platforms also give health‑based guidance (e.g., “sensitive groups should limit prolonged exertion”). Feel free to let me know if you’d like a quick summary of what each pollutant means or how to interpret the AQI scale!
